subject: Dedicated capacity SKU plan for Veridian AI - H100 / A100 / L4 mix
messages:

Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing kickoff for Veridian - workload details?

Hi Anika,

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, the next step for us is to map your workload profile to a SKU mix recommendation for Dedicated (H100 / A100 / L4). To make sure our proposal is tight for procurement, can you confirm the following by EOD: 

- Percent of requests that are long-context generation (>8k tokens) vs short-generation (<=2k) vs embeddings/reranking.
- Average batch sizes you expect for embeddings and for generation.
- Latency SLOs (p50/p95) for the user-facing paths.
- Any firm constraints on on-prem vs hosted hardware for compliance.

I attached the minimal workload profile CSV you can fill — that will let us run a quick cost/throughput simulation and suggest a reserve.

I'll loop in Kimberly for the SKU tradeoffs and Priyom for ops sizing.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Anika Rao <anika@veridian.ai>

Date: 2027-04-01T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing kickoff for Veridian - workload details?

Hi Diego — thanks, attaching the filled profile. High level:

- Long-context generation (>8k): ~18% of traffic (summary and code-gen tasks for enterprise users).
- Short-generation (<=2k): ~52% of traffic (chatbots and quick generation).
- Embeddings/reranking: ~30% (heavy use, many small requests, batch size typically 64 for embeddings).
- Latency SLOs: user-facing p50 < 200ms, p95 < 700ms for short-generation; for long-context p95 we can accept up to 1.8s in heavy tails.
- No on-prem requirement for this initial phase; must be in a VPC in us-west.

We have a target monthly committed spend of ~$85k/month for the first-year reserved pool; procurement is on a 60-day cadence. Procurement contact is procurement@veridian.ai.

Anika
Head of Platform
Veridian AI

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing kickoff for Veridian - SKU recommendations and risks

Thanks for the profile, Anika — below is a pragmatic SKU mix and the rationale. I focused on meeting the p95 SLOs while keeping within the target commit range; numbers are conservative and assume moderate caching + prefix reuse.

Recommendation (initial reserved pool):
- H100 (NVIDIA H100 80GB) x8 nodes (heavy long-context models): handles ~18% long-context traffic. Rationale: H100's memory + FP8 throughput is needed for 16k+ context models and large batch KV cache retention. Without H100 you'll see either higher latency or need expensive tiling.
- A100 (NVIDIA A100 80GB) x10 nodes (balanced generation throughput): for short-generation where throughput and mixed-precision performance matter; cheaper than H100 on list price and well-understood for batched workloads.
- L4 (NVIDIA L4) x28 nodes (embeddings & low-latency fan-out): optimized for embeddings and many small requests with very low tokens-per-second cost; use for reranking, semantic search, and cheap chat fallbacks.

Estimated operational outcomes (based on your profile):
- Aggregate token throughput headroom ~ 1.35x on target volumes with the pool above (gives room for spikes).
- Expected p95 short-generation latency: ~300-450ms (including network and infra overhead) with request routing favoring L4 for cheap short calls and A100 for batched synthesis.
- Expected p95 long-context latency: ~900ms - 1.6s depending on model choice; H100 prevents tail blowups for very large contexts.

Cost & reserve fit:
- This mix maps to an estimated committed spend of $78k–$92k/month depending on discount and utilization assumptions. I'll attach the cost model (sku_cost_model.xlsx) with toggles for utilization (40/60/80%) and quantization options (INT8 / FP16 / FP8 where available).

Operational notes & fallback policies:
- Fallback path: L4 pool should be used for stateless embeddings and cheap chat fallbacks; we recommend automatic model variant fallback (3 alternatives) if H100 queueing > 2s.
- Cache strategy: prefix caching for conversational flows and KV caching for long-context generation — set TTLs conservative (12–24h) to maximize reuse without stale-safety issues.
- Quantization: for most long-context models, prefer FP8 on H100 for best perf/memory. A100 + INT8 quant profiles can reduce memory pressure but may require model validation.
- Autoscaling: use scheduled scale-up for predictable daytime usage and a burst pool for transient spikes tied to routing policies.

Open risks:
- If committed utilization lands < 45%, unit economics will degrade; consider a smaller initial H100 footprint and fast path to scale if utilization exceeds expectations.
- Procurement timeline (~60 days) means we should recommend a conservative initial reserve and a clear expansion clause.

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether Veridian wants H100-capable private nodes or H100 via dedicated-hosted instances (impacts pricing/ops).
2) I'll push the detailed cost model and fallthrough playbook.
3) Diego/Ben — if this looks good I'll ask procurement to draft an LOI and reservation sizing for Q2 start.

Attachments: sku_cost_model.xlsx, fallthrough_playbook.pdf

-Kim
